# Idempotent Loading

A load script is **idempotent** when running it twice leaves the store exactly as running it once did.
This is the difference between a script you can re-run while developing and a script you must
remember to precede with a manual wipe.

Two repositories solve it two ways, and the pairing is what makes the concept transferable — this
is one of the few concepts spanning both [[python-programming-laboratories]] and
[[discrete-mathematics-laboratories]].

## Relational: constraint plus conflict clause

```sql
UNIQUE(context, knowledge, response)
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO ...
```

The **database** enforces the identity; the insert declares what to do when it is violated. Lab 13
loads 610 rows; the second run inserts 0. That number is the test — an idempotent loader is one you
can *observe* being idempotent, which is why the row count is reported rather than assumed.

The critical part is that uniqueness lives in the schema, not in the loader. A loader-side
"check then insert" is a race and a lie: it works until two processes run it. `INSERT OR IGNORE`
delegates the decision to the only component that can make it atomically. See [[sqlite]].

## Graph: MERGE plus uniqueness constraints

[[cypher]]'s `MERGE` is match-or-create against a pattern. Lab 6 uses it with node uniqueness
constraints so that re-running the `LOAD CSV` import re-attaches to existing nodes instead of
duplicating them — one `:Object` per CSV row regardless of how many times the script runs. The repo
records the payoff explicitly when the dataset count was corrected:

> "**Data note.** The dataset holds **39** countries; earlier drafts of the guide said 38 (and 950
> `HAS_VALUE`). The numbers were corrected to **39 objects / 975 edges** throughout — the import
> logic itself was already correct (it `MERGE`s one object per row)."
> — Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories/lab6_Neo4j/README.md, 2026-07-10

The documentation was wrong; the loader was not. That is exactly what idempotence buys — the fix was
a text edit, not a reload. See [[pawlak-information-system]] and [[neo4j]].

## The general rule

- Declare the **natural key** in the schema (`UNIQUE`, a node constraint), never only in the loader.
- Make the write express its conflict behaviour (`INSERT OR IGNORE`, `MERGE`, `ON CONFLICT`).
- **Report what changed** — rows inserted, nodes merged — so the second run *demonstrates* zero work
  rather than merely not crashing.

## Contrast

[[data-warehousing-and-business-intelligence]] approaches the same problem from the verification side
rather than the constraint side. Both are answers to "how do I know the load is right?"; only the
constraint version survives being run by someone who forgot to check.
